accepted.question_text: Let X be the feature space, let the binary label set be {-1, +1}, let D = {(x^(l), y^(l))}_{l=1}^m be a dataset sampled from a probability space (D, Sigma, P), and let H be a weak-hypothesis class that is AdaBoost-natural with respect to D, meaning that H contains the constant classifier h(x) = 1, is closed under negation, and every h in H misclassifies at least one example in D. For Optimal AdaBoost, let w_t in Delta_m denote the example-weight distribution at round t, let err(h; w, D) = sum_{l=1}^m w(l) 1[h(x^(l)) != y^(l)], and let H(w_t, D) = arg min_{h in H} err(h; w_t, D), with the weak learner using a deterministic tie-breaking rule to select a representative hypothesis. Is it true that for mu-almost all probability spaces (D, Sigma, P), for any dataset D sampled from P, and for mu-almost all such H, there exist m_0, T_0 > 0 such that whenever m > m_0, then P-almost surely, for every t > T_0, either H(w_t, D) contains exactly one hypothesis, or every pair of hypotheses in H(w_t, D) agrees on all training examples in D, or the total w_t-weight of the training examples on which two tied optimal hypotheses disagree converges to 0 as t tends to infinity?

evidence.quote: We denote the set of hypotheses that the weak learner that AdaBoost uses, or simply the weak-hypothesis class, by H. We say that H is AdaBoost-natural with respect to D if (1) the hypothesis h, such that, for all x in X, h(x) = 1, is in H; (2) if h in H, then -h in H; and (3) for all h in H, there exists an (x, y) in D such that h(x) != y.

We also assume that the weak learner has a deterministic tie-braking rule; i.e., denoting err(h; w, D) ... and H(w, D) equiv arg min_{h in H} err(h; w, D), for every example weight w that AdaBoost could generate, the weak learner always outputs the same weak hypothesis h* in H(w, D).

Conjecture 1 (No-Ties Conjecture) For mu-almost all probability spaces (D, Sigma, P) and any dataset D ~ P, and mu-almost all H that are AdaBoost-natural with respect to D, there exist m0, T0 > 0, such that if m > m0 is the size of D, then, P-almost surely, either (1), for all t > T0 rounds of Optimal AdaBoost, either (1.a) |H(wt, D)| = 1; or (1.b) for all pairs ht, h't in H(wt, D), ht(x^(l)) = h't(x^(l)) for all l = 1, ..., m; or (2) lim_{t->infty} sum_{l=1}^m wt(l) 1[ht(x^(l)) != h't(x^(l))] = 0, where ht, h't in H(wt, D).

accepted.question_text: In the same Optimal AdaBoost setting where D = {(x^(l), y^(l))}_{l=1}^m is sampled from a probability space (D, Sigma, P), H is AdaBoost-natural with respect to D, and the classifier is obtained after T rounds of the standard binary-classification AdaBoost procedure, is it true that for mu-almost all probability spaces (D, Sigma, P), for any dataset D sampled from P, and for mu-almost all such H, there exist m_0, T_0 > 0 such that whenever m > m_0 and T > T_0, the decision boundary of the binary classifier output by Optimal AdaBoost after T rounds on D has P-measure zero?

We say that H is AdaBoost-natural with respect to D if (1) the hypothesis h, such that, for all x in X, h(x) = 1, is in H; (2) if h in H, then -h in H; and (3) for all h in H, there exists an (x, y) in D such that h(x) != y.

Conjecture 2 (Measure-Zero-Decision-Boundary Conjecture) For mu-almost all probability spaces (D, Sigma, P) and any dataset D ~ P, and mu-almost all H that are AdaBoost-natural with respect to D, there exist m0, T0 > 0, such that if m > m0, and T > T0 is the total number of rounds of Optimal AdaBoost, then the decision boundary of the binary classifier that Optimal AdaBoost outputs after T rounds when given dataset D as input has P-measure zero.

accepted.question_text: In the same decision-stump setting where X = [0, 1]^n, H_b is the midpoint-rule stump class induced by the dataset, E_b is the effective stump set obtained after removing dominated stumps, and U_b^T = union_{t=1}^T {h_t} is the set of unique decision stumps selected by Optimal AdaBoost from E_b during T rounds, is it true that for mu-almost all probability spaces (D, Sigma, P) and any dataset D sampled from P, there exist m_0, T_0 > 0 such that whenever m > m_0 and T > T_0, the conditional expectation E[|U_b^T| | D] is bounded above by (log T + 1)^c for some c in [1, 2), P-almost surely?

evidence.quote: Further, denote by U_b^T equiv union_{t=1}^T {h_t} the set of unique decision stumps actually selected by Optimal AdaBoost from E_b after T rounds.

Conjecture 4 (Logarithmic Growth on Unique Stumps) For mu-almost all probability spaces (D, Sigma, P) and any dataset D ~ P, there exist m0, T0 > 0, such that if m > m0 and T > T0, we have E[ |U_b^T| | D ] <= (log T + 1)^c, for some c in [1, 2), P-almost surely.

accepted.question_text: Consider the decision-stump specialization of Optimal AdaBoost in which the feature space is X = [0, 1]^n and the labeled example space is D = [0, 1]^n x {-1, +1}. Let H_hat be the finite set of decision stumps induced on a finite dataset D by the midpoint rule: for each feature dimension i, project D along that dimension and, whenever two distinct consecutive examples have different labels, create a stump using the midpoint x'_i = (x_i^(l_j) + x_i^(l_{j+1})) / 2 and h(x) = sign(x_i - x'_i). Remove every dominated hypothesis h in H_hat for which there exists another h' in H_hat such that h'(x^(l)) != y^(l) implies h(x^(l)) != y^(l) for every l = 1, ..., m, and call the resulting effective set E_hat. Let U_hat^T = union_{t=1}^T {h_t} be the set of unique decision stumps actually selected by Optimal AdaBoost from E_hat after T rounds. Given a measurable space (D, Sigma, P), a dataset D sampled from P, and the number of rounds T, provide non-trivial upper and lower bounds on |H_hat|, |E_hat|, and |U_hat^T|.
accepted.context_brief: Bounds on effective and selected stumps

evidence.quote: For simplicity, we concentrate on the feature space X = [0,1]^n, the n-dimensional hypercube, so that D = [0,1]^n x {-1,+1}. Denote by H the finite set of decision stumps on the finite dataset D induced by using the so-called midpoint rule. In this rule, we project D along each feature dimension i and create a decision stump h based on the midpoint between any pair of distinct consecutive examples.

We eliminate from H any dominated hypothesis; that is, we do not need to consider any h in H, such that there exists another h' in H, with the property that h'(x^(l)) != y^(l) implies h(x^(l)) != y^(l) for all l = 1, ..., m. Denote the resulting effective set by E. Further, denote by U^T equiv union_{t=1}^T {h_t} the set of unique decision stumps actually selected by Optimal AdaBoost from E after T rounds.

Problem 1 (Bounding the Number of Effective Stumps) Given a measurable space (D, Sigma, P), a dataset D ~ P, and the number of rounds of Optimal AdaBoost T. Provide non-trivial upper and lower bounds on |H|, |E|, and |U^T|.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Conjecture 3 (Constructive-Proof Conjecture) For mu-almost all probability spaces (D, Sigma, P) and any dataset D ~ P, and mu-almost all H that are AdaBoost-natural with respect to D, there exists m0 > 0, such that if m > m0, then there exists a constructive proof of existence of a measure for which the Optimal AdaBoost weight update is measure-preserving, P-almost surely.

evidence.quote: In our work, we study Optimal AdaBoost as a dynamical system of the weights w over the examples in D; we also refer to such w as the example or sample weights. In particular, we take a dynamical system view to the Optimal AdaBoost update rule of the example weights w on D. That is, each w is a probability distribution over the m examples in D.

In our work we employ tools from ergodic theory to establish our convergence results. We provide a non-constructive proof of the existence of a measure for which the Optimal-AdaBoost update is measure-preserving.

Conjecture 3 (Constructive-Proof Conjecture) For mu-almost all probability spaces (D, Sigma, P) and any dataset D ~ P, and mu-almost all H that are AdaBoost-natural with respect to D, there exists m0 > 0, such that if m > m0, then there exists a constructive proof of existence of a measure for which the Optimal AdaBoost weight update is measure-preserving, P-almost surely.
